plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and payment at the second-highest bid. Since there's no history, I'll assume a standard optimal strategy for a second-price auction. Bidding my true value is a dominant strategy in a second-price auction, as it maximizes my utility regardless of what others bid. My value is $25.

I will bid slightly above what I anticipate the second-highest bid to be, given my value. Since my value is $17, I need to ensure I win if the second-highest bid is below $17. I will consider a bid that is a significant fraction of my value, but not so high as to risk overpaying. A bid of 0.8 * value is a good starting point, but I will adjust it slightly to be competitive.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such an auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding below my value risks losing a profitable opportunity, while bidding above my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. Since this is the first and only round, and values are independently redrawn, there's no history to learn from for this specific value. I will bid my true value.
